newsitem.title: CANADA: BC Sugar agrees to C$415 million surprise bid.
newsitem.headline: BC Sugar agrees to C$415 million surprise bid.

text.p: The tug-of-war for BC Sugar Refinery Ltd. took a surprise turn Thursday when the company accepted a last-minute C$415 million ($307 million) bid from Vancouver businessman Stuart Belkin and Toronto's Onex Corp.
Belkin and Vancouver financier Jim Pattison have for months been locked in competition for BC Sugar, which controls about 70 percent of Canada's sugar market.
In a surprising twist, Pattison agreed to tender his 28 percent stake to the C$16.50 ($12.22) a share offer. BC Sugar operates sugar refineries across Canada and in New York.
The takeover battle appeared to have been decided in Pattison's favour earlier this month when BC Sugar recommended his C$15 ($11.11) a share or C$266 million ($197 million) takeover offer.
But Belkin joined with Toronto-based Onex to come back at the eleventh hour with the new offer that won approval from both BC Sugar and Pattison.
The deal was announced on Thursday just hours before Pattison's bid had been due to expire.
"I am not a quitter," Belkin said in explaining why he persisted until the last minute. "I was not keen to throw in the towel."
Nick Desmarais, a top Pattison adviser, declined to say why his group dropped out of the bidding or if it felt the higher price tag was justified.

But Pattison, who has diverse holdings in car dealerships, consumer products and a Vancouver coal terminal, will pocket a C$5 million ($3.7 million) kill fee and a tidy profit on his 28 percent stake in BC Sugar.
"We are satisfied with the price. We're going to tender our shares and we wish them well," said Desmarais, who added that Pattison harboured no bitterness after the battle.

Belkin, who has investments in real estate, a gasoline retailer and waste management, said he decided to join forces with Onex because he did not have the financial resources to attempt a full takeover bid on his own.
Onex owns a diverse collection of businesses with revenues of C$11 billion and has a reputation for shrewd investments.

Onex will own 75 percent of BC Sugar and Belkin's Balaclava the rest. The takeover will be financed through a combination of bank loans and equity and the offer is expected to expire on July 29. It is conditioned on two-thirds of BC Sugar's shares being tendered.
Analysts were surprised by the latest turn but said the C$1.50 a share increase in price and Pattison's decision to tender to the offer assure Balaclava and Onex victory.
"It has come to an end now. They will get control," said Goepel Shields analyst Carl Hoyt.

Belkin's Balaclava Enterprises had previously offered about C$118 million ($88 milion) to acquire 32 percent of BC Sugar. Combined with the 20 percent he already owned, this would have given him control of the company.
But shareholders reacted negatively to that proposal because they wanted a takeover offer for the all the shares. That response allowed Pattison to win backing for his bid.
